items: SEC 8-K (filed 2026-11-12): on 2026-11-11 the Board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as President, CEO and director, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress (age 59, CFO since 2013) appointed interim CEO while remaining CFO; board search for a permanent CEO (internal and external). Harvey C. Jones (age 73, director since 1993) appointed first-ever Chair. The 8-K gives no reason for the resignation.
Huang agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving (CNBC via Reuters). Interim CEO Kress gathering the executive team at HQ.
Market reaction 2026-11-12: NVDA opened 151.005, low 148.80, then recovered to ~164 on ~499M shares; AMD and Broadcom up to ~5% on the news; US indices reversed higher.
Context: resignation came three days after the board opened its investigation and amid a DOJ inquiry and congressional pressure; Fortune (2026-11-09) noted no telegraphed succession plan.
Huang acknowledged a relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed director (Mar-Nov 2023).
Board opened an independent investigation (Wachtell Lipton) into whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
Reported DOJ inquiry into whether Singapore-based Megaspeed routed Nvidia chips to China; ~240,000 chips / $7.5bn alleged; Megaspeed denies.
NYT: Commerce (BIS) Megaspeed probe moved to DOJ after Nvidia's general counsel contacted investigators; investigation continues.
No public finding that Nvidia knowingly violated export controls; no charges against Huang reported.
GOP Senator Kevin Cramer called for Huang's resignation; push for chip-export restrictions revived on Capitol Hill.
Earlier 2026 context: Super Micro-linked smuggling charges; Senators Warren and Banks asked Commerce to review Nvidia export licences (Mar 2026); Oct 1 DOJ arrest in a $300m server smuggling case.
China rejects espionage allegations. Analysts cut price targets; Wedbush flags key-person risk. Michael Burry calls NVDA 'a heck of a trade'.
